questions.question_text: Which component performs most arithmetic and logical operations in a computer?
questions.explanation: The CPU executes instructions and performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes data?

options.label: B
options.text: Raw facts that can be processed

questions.explanation: Data consists of raw facts that can be processed into useful information.

questions.question_text: One byte is equal to:
questions.explanation: A byte conventionally consists of eight bits.

questions.question_text: Which number system uses only 0 and 1?
questions.explanation: Binary represents values using the two digits 0 and 1.

questions.question_text: Software is best described as:

options.label: A
options.text: The physical parts of a computer

options.label: B
options.text: Programs and instructions used by a computer

options.label: D
options.text: Electrical power supplied to a computer

questions.explanation: Software consists of programs and instructions that direct computer operations.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes information from data?

options.label: A
options.text: Information is processed data with meaning

options.label: B
options.text: Data is always more useful than information

questions.explanation: Information is data that has been processed or organised into a meaningful form.

questions.question_text: Which device is primarily used for entering text into a computer?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device commonly used to enter text and commands.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.explanation: A monitor displays visual output produced by the computer.

questions.question_text: Which device can convert printed documents into digital form?
questions.explanation: A scanner captures printed text or images and converts them into digital data.

questions.question_text: RAM is mainly used to:

options.label: B
options.text: Hold data and programs currently in use

questions.explanation: RAM temporarily holds active programs and data for fast processor access.

questions.question_text: Which storage device normally has no moving mechanical parts?
questions.explanation: SSDs use flash memory and generally contain no moving mechanical parts.

questions.question_text: A peripheral device is best described as:

options.label: A
options.text: A device connected to a computer to provide input, output, storage, or communication functions

questions.explanation: Peripherals extend the capabilities of a computer through input, output, storage, or communication.

questions.question_text: The main purpose of an operating system is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Manage computer hardware and provide services for applications

questions.explanation: An operating system manages hardware resources and provides an environment for applications.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an operating system?
questions.explanation: Windows is an operating system, while the others are application programs.

questions.question_text: A folder is mainly used to:
questions.explanation: Folders help users organise files and subfolders logically.

questions.question_text: Which file extension commonly represents a PDF document?
questions.explanation: The .pdf extension commonly identifies Portable Document Format files.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of a file path?

options.label: A
options.text: To identify the location of a file or folder

questions.explanation: A file path describes where a file or directory is located within a storage hierarchy.

questions.question_text: Why is a clear file-naming convention useful in academic work?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes files easier to identify, sort, and retrieve

options.label: C
options.text: It prevents every form of data loss

options.label: D
options.text: It removes the need for backups

questions.explanation: Consistent file naming improves organisation and retrieval, especially when many documents are involved.

questions.question_text: The Internet is best described as:

options.label: A
options.text: A global network of interconnected computer networks

questions.explanation: The Internet links many computer networks around the world.

questions.question_text: Which application is primarily used to access websites?
questions.explanation: A web browser retrieves and displays web resources.

questions.question_text: What does URL stand for?
questions.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator and identifies the location of a resource on the web.

questions.question_text: HTTPS is generally preferred to HTTP because it:

options.label: A
options.text: Encrypts communication between browser and server

questions.explanation: HTTPS uses encryption to protect data in transit between a browser and a server.

questions.question_text: A search engine is used primarily to:

options.label: A
options.text: Find information and resources on the web

questions.explanation: Search engines index web content and help users locate relevant resources.

questions.question_text: Which search query would usually give the most focused academic results?

options.label: B
options.text: climate change renewable energy Nigeria university study

questions.explanation: Specific keywords and concepts usually produce more focused and relevant search results.

questions.question_text: Which field identifies the main recipient of an email?
questions.explanation: The To field contains the primary recipient's email address.

questions.question_text: The subject line of an email should ideally:

options.label: A
options.text: Briefly describe the purpose of the message

questions.explanation: A clear subject line helps the recipient understand the purpose of the message quickly.

questions.question_text: BCC is useful when:

options.label: A
options.text: Recipients should not see one another's email addresses

options.label: B
options.text: An email must be deleted immediately

options.label: C
options.text: A file needs to be compressed

options.label: D
options.text: The computer has no internet connection

questions.explanation: BCC hides recipients' addresses from the other recipients of the same message.

questions.question_text: Which behaviour is most appropriate in a formal academic email?

options.label: A
options.text: Using a clear greeting, concise message, and appropriate closing

questions.explanation: Professional email communication should be clear, respectful, and appropriately structured.

questions.question_text: An email attachment is:

options.label: A
options.text: A file sent together with an email message

questions.explanation: Attachments allow files such as documents or images to accompany an email.

questions.question_text: Why should unexpected email attachments be treated cautiously?

options.label: A
options.text: They may contain malicious software or phishing content

options.label: C
options.text: They automatically delete the operating system

questions.explanation: Unexpected attachments can carry malware or form part of phishing attacks.

questions.question_text: Which application is primarily designed for creating and editing text documents?
questions.explanation: Word processors are designed for creating, formatting, and editing text documents.

questions.question_text: Which formatting feature changes the appearance of characters?
questions.explanation: Font settings affect typeface, size, style, and related character appearance.

questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of spell-checking software?
questions.explanation: Spell checkers identify words that may be misspelled and suggest corrections.

questions.question_text: Using styles in a long document is useful because styles:

options.label: A
options.text: Provide consistent formatting for headings and other elements

questions.explanation: Styles make formatting consistent and help structure long documents efficiently.

questions.question_text: A page break is used to:

options.label: A
options.text: Force subsequent content to begin on a new page

questions.explanation: A page break explicitly moves following content to the next page.

questions.question_text: Why is using automatic headings preferable to manually making headings bold in a long academic document?

options.label: A
options.text: Automatic headings support consistent formatting and features such as navigation and tables of contents

options.label: D
options.text: Automatic headings reduce every document to one page

questions.explanation: Structured heading styles support consistency and document-navigation features.

questions.question_text: A spreadsheet organises data mainly into:
questions.explanation: Spreadsheet worksheets organise information into rows and columns.

questions.question_text: The intersection of a row and a column is called a:
questions.explanation: A cell is formed where a row and column intersect.

questions.question_text: Which symbol usually begins a spreadsheet formula?
questions.explanation: Spreadsheet formulas normally begin with an equals sign.

questions.question_text: What does the formula =SUM(A1:A5) do?

options.label: A
options.text: Adds the values in cells A1 through A5

questions.explanation: SUM adds the numerical values within the specified range.

questions.question_text: Which chart is often suitable for comparing values across categories?
questions.explanation: Bar charts are effective for comparing quantities across discrete categories.

questions.question_text: Why is an absolute cell reference useful in a spreadsheet?

options.label: A
options.text: It keeps a referenced cell fixed when a formula is copied

options.label: B
options.text: It prevents a workbook from being opened

options.label: C
options.text: It converts every number to text

options.label: D
options.text: It removes the need for formulas

questions.explanation: Absolute references, such as $A$1, remain fixed when formulas are copied to other cells.

questions.question_text: Presentation software is mainly used to:
questions.explanation: Presentation software helps create visual slide-based presentations.

questions.question_text: A slide layout controls:

options.label: A
options.text: The arrangement of placeholders and content on a slide

questions.explanation: Slide layouts determine how titles, text, images, and other placeholders are arranged.

questions.question_text: Which practice usually improves presentation readability?

options.label: A
options.text: Using concise text and sufficiently large fonts

options.label: B
options.text: Filling every slide with long paragraphs

questions.explanation: Concise text and readable fonts make presentation content easier for an audience to follow.

questions.question_text: A slide transition controls:

options.label: A
options.text: How one slide changes to the next

options.label: B
options.text: How a spreadsheet formula is calculated

options.label: C
options.text: How files are stored on disk

options.label: D
options.text: How an email recipient is selected

questions.explanation: Transitions determine the visual effect used when moving between slides.

questions.question_text: Why should animations be used selectively in academic presentations?

options.label: A
options.text: Excessive animation can distract from the content

options.label: C
options.text: Animations prevent text from being displayed

questions.explanation: Animations can support communication, but excessive use can distract the audience.

questions.question_text: Which approach best supports an oral presentation?

options.label: A
options.text: Slides summarise key points while the presenter explains them

options.label: B
options.text: The presenter reads every word from densely packed slides

options.label: C
options.text: Every slide contains several full textbook pages

options.label: D
options.text: The presenter avoids explaining visual information

questions.explanation: Slides should support rather than replace the speaker's explanation.

questions.question_text: Information literacy involves the ability to:

options.label: A
options.text: Find, evaluate, and use information effectively

options.label: B
options.text: Type faster than every other user

questions.explanation: Information literacy includes locating, evaluating, and responsibly using information.

questions.question_text: Which source is generally most appropriate for academic research?
questions.explanation: Peer-reviewed research is generally more suitable for academic work because its methods and claims are scrutinised.

questions.question_text: Why should the publication date of an online source be checked?

options.label: A
options.text: To assess whether the information is current enough for the topic

options.label: B
options.text: To determine the colour of the website

questions.explanation: Publication date helps determine whether information is sufficiently current for the research question.

questions.question_text: A citation is used primarily to:

options.label: A
options.text: Acknowledge the source of information or ideas

options.label: B
options.text: Hide the identity of the author

options.label: C
options.text: Increase the size of a document

questions.explanation: Citations acknowledge sources and help readers locate the referenced material.

questions.question_text: Plagiarism occurs when a student:

options.label: A
options.text: Presents another person's words or ideas as their own without proper acknowledgement

questions.explanation: Plagiarism involves using another person's work without appropriate attribution.

questions.question_text: When evaluating a website for academic use, which combination is most important?

options.label: A
options.text: Authority, evidence, relevance, currency, and purpose

questions.explanation: Credibility depends on who produced the information, the supporting evidence, relevance, currency, and purpose.

topics.name: Cybersecurity, Digital Safety and Study Productivity

questions.question_text: Which password is generally strongest?
questions.explanation: A strong password is long, unpredictable, and uses a varied combination of characters.

questions.question_text: Phishing is an attempt to:

options.label: A
options.text: Trick users into revealing sensitive information

questions.explanation: Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to obtain passwords, financial information, or other sensitive data.

questions.question_text: Two-factor authentication improves account security by:

options.label: A
options.text: Requiring an additional verification factor beyond the password

options.label: B
options.text: Removing the need for any login credentials

options.label: D
options.text: Allowing anyone to access the account

questions.explanation: Two-factor authentication requires more than one form of verification.

questions.question_text: Which backup practice provides better protection against data loss?

options.label: A
options.text: Keeping copies in more than one reliable location

options.label: B
options.text: Saving the only copy on one device

questions.explanation: Multiple reliable copies reduce the risk that a single device failure will destroy important work.

questions.question_text: Which study strategy is generally more effective than repeatedly rereading the same notes?

options.label: B
options.text: Studying continuously without breaks for many hours

options.label: C
options.text: Copying notes word for word repeatedly

questions.explanation: Active recall and spaced practice strengthen retrieval and long-term retention.

questions.question_text: A student receives a message claiming to be from the university and requesting an immediate password reset through an unfamiliar link. What is the safest response?

options.label: C
options.text: Verify the request through an official university channel before taking action

questions.explanation: Unexpected credential requests should be independently verified through a trusted official channel before any sensitive information is entered.
